Optional flags:
- `--from N` — start from phase N instead of the first incomplete phase.
- `--to N` — stop after phase N completes (halt instead of advancing to next phase).
- `--only N` — execute only phase N (single-phase mode).
- `--interactive` — run discuss inline with questions (not auto-answered), then dispatch plan→execute as background agents. Keeps the main context lean while preserving user input on decisions.

- `--converge` — run each phase's planning step through `gsd-plan-review-convergence` instead of plain `gsd-plan-phase`. Works even when `workflow.plan_review_convergence` is `false` — the explicit flag overrides the gate; the gate (`workflow.plan_review_convergence=true` enables it) governs the standalone `gsd-plan-review-convergence` command. Without the flag, planning runs `gsd-plan-phase`.
- `--cross-ai` — compatibility alias for `--converge`.

When `--converge` or `--cross-ai` is set, reviewer selector flags supported by `gsd-plan-review-convergence` may be passed through: `--codex`, `--claude`, `--opencode`, `--ollama`, `--lm-studio`, `--llama-cpp`, `--all`, and `--max-cycles N`.
Project context, phase list, and state are resolved inside the workflow using init commands (`specforge gsd progress-report`, `specforge query`). No upfront context loading needed.

In the shell blocks above, `$MILESTONE` is `v1.0` and `$PROJECT` is `taskboard`.
## What runs here and what does not
This workflow runs in this conversation, one phase after another, through the prompt steps above. Each step keeps its own gate: a phase that is not ready is refused there, and you stop and report it.
- The unattended harness (`specforged`) is not part of `@gsd/core`. Nothing starts this workflow by itself or resumes it after the conversation ends.
- `--from`, `--to` and `--only` are phase numbers of the milestone `$MILESTONE` named above (the one still open): a phase of another milestone is not a bound here.
- `claude_orchestration.*` and `external_job.*` are declared settings with no effect here, even when the settings block above shows them set.
- `/gsd-code-review` and the UI gate (`check ui-plan-gate`) belong to extensions that are not installed: skip the code review and the UI design contract, and say so.

files it talks about are entities of the project's spec here, and the tools it calls are SpecForge's. This section says
where each thing went; where it and the workflow disagree, this section wins.

Read an entity with `specforge query <id> [--kinds <kind>] [--depth <n>] [--format json]` (MCP tool `specforge.query`).
Check the spec with `specforge check`. Create and edit with `specforge new <kind> <id> ...`, `specforge set`,
`specforge unset` and `specforge link`, or the MCP tool `specforge.edit`. An artifact is created with
`specforge new artifact <id> "<title>" --in <file> --plan <plan> --field path=<file>` (or `specforge.edit`).
## How to work
- **Computed is never written.** A status, a progress, a position and a count are computed from the graph. Where the
workflow says to update one, there is nothing to do.
- **Harness fields have one writer**: the command of `@gsd/core` that owns them (`specforge gsd <command>`; `specforge gsd help` lists them), never `specforge set`.
- **A command step's line has no arguments.** The step names the command; this text gives its arguments. Every
`--by` names who answers: `--by "<user>"` for a person, the agent's name for an agent.
- **Judges record their own verdicts** with `specforge gsd record-verdict` (the agent's body says how). An
orchestrator never records a verdict on a judge's behalf.
- **A refused call** (`gate_failed`, `human_only`, `stale_revision`, `invalid_input`) is reported to the user with its
message. Never edit the spec to get around it.
- **An agent this host does not have installed** (`gsd-debugger`, `gsd-ui-researcher`, `gsd-ui-checker`,
`gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-codebase-mapper`, ...) is skipped, and the skip is said.
- **Spawning an agent** on this host: as the adapter header above says (the agent is the installed `gsd-<name>`). The model is the installed agent's own: skip any model resolution.
- **References** the workflow names are read with `specforge gsd reference <path>`.
- **Ids in the shell blocks.** `$PHASE_ID` and `$PLAN_ID` are the entity the run is about (the end of this text names
it), `$MILESTONE` is the current milestone and `$PROJECT` the project (the end of this text names them too).
